top_story: By 11 July, the sharpest regional shift was the collapse of the brief US-Iran truce into open retaliation, after two consecutive nights of US strikes and Iranian attacks on American bases in the Gulf on 9 July were followed by fresh threats from Trump during Khamenei’s funeral and burial. The funeral became more than a symbolic moment, hardening confrontation and narrowing space for diplomacy as both sides folded domestic mobilization and deterrent signaling into the crisis. In the occupied West Bank, Israel’s 10 July move to seize Palestinian land to widen Route 60 advanced a separate but connected logic of coercion, deepening territorial fragmentation around Ramallah and Nablus as regional attention fixed on the US-Iran clash. The combined effect is a more combustible regional environment in which interstate escalation and entrenching occupation reinforce civilian insecurity and further erode political off-ramps.
